sources.title: Unicode CLDR as a versioned external locale-data component
sources.sections_read: What is CLDR; main components; How to Use
sources.confirmed: CLDR separates locale data and its specification from implementing libraries. It documents locale-sensitive date/number/currency/unit formatting and plural rules, and links release downloads.
sources.limits: Data alone does not supply application translations or a complete runtime; current feature coverage is not all backdated to version 25. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: unknown. Original read and any failures remain in runs/B/C20.json.

sources.title: Globalize modular formatting with externally supplied CLDR data
sources.sections_read: README: Design Goals; CLDR data; modular loading; Compilation and Runtime modules
sources.confirmed: Globalize keeps locale data outside the library, allows selective modules and locales, and can compile formatters to a smaller runtime. The current README supplies implementation design evidence but not a verified pre-cutoff version.
sources.limits: Applications manage modules and matching data; this JavaScript architecture is a transfer example, with current features not dated before the cutoff. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: unknown. Original read and any failures remain in runs/B/C20.json.

sources.title: messageformat compiler and runtime separation
sources.confirmed: The repository describes compiling MessageFormat strings to JavaScript functions, with separate parser, CLI, loaders, and runtime dependencies. Only this library architecture is used; other products mentioned there are not new discoveries.
sources.limits: The implementation targets JavaScript; Rust would need analogous tooling or integration, and current packages have unverified historical dates. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: unknown. Original read and any failures remain in runs/B/C20.json.

sources.title: i18n.html
sources.sections_read: How I18n works; translation/localize API; Simple and alternate backends; pluralization
sources.confirmed: I18n separates a public translate/localize API from swappable backends. The default backend's English-oriented limits are explicit, while richer backends and locale-specific plural rules are supported.
sources.limits: This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: unknown. Original read and any failures remain in runs/B/C20.json.

sources.title: Intl.js
sources.confirmed: Intl.js is an unmaintained compatibility implementation of ECMA-402. Its README names the standard's December 2012 first edition, separates locale data from library code, and has a 2013 copyright, but these do not date the currently documented implementation features.
sources.limits: This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: unknown. Original read and any failures remain in runs/B/C20.json.

sources.title: icu.unicode.org
sources.sections_read: ICU services; Why ICU4C; Why ICU4J; User Guide link
sources.confirmed: ICU supplies locale formatting, collation, calendar and bidi behavior through C/C++ and Java libraries. Its project page motivates a portable external foundation and updating internationalization independently of Java's release schedule.

sources.title: ICU MessageFormat
sources.sections_read: Overview; MessageFormat; complex arguments; argument formatting
sources.confirmed: ICU's guide recommends translating complete messages, supports plural and select branches, and permits formatting parameters separately before message assembly. It notes changes introduced in ICU 4.8, but no corresponding calendar date was verified.
sources.limits: Requires library and locale-data integration; the full currently documented behavior was not verified in a dated pre-cutoff snapshot. sources.sections_read: Introduction; How I18n works; Overall Architecture; Public I18n API

sources.title: ECMA-402 first-edition internationalization API
sources.sections_read: Article date; design goals; API functionality and omissions
sources.confirmed: Dated 2012-12-18, the original working-group participant's article describes ECMA-402 as a separately adoptable extension exposing existing internationalization libraries. Its first edition deliberately limits itself to collation and number/date formatting; resource loading and message construction are outside that edition.
sources.limits: The first edition omits resource loading and message construction; this boundary is not a complete localization solution. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: pre_decision. Original read and any failures remain in runs/B/C20.json.

sources.title: Jed gettext-style lookup followed by interpolation
sources.sections_read: API; locale data; positional interpolation; Translation files; Why gettext
sources.confirmed: Jed selects translated messages by domain, context and locale plural metadata, then interpolates reordered values with sprintf. It consumes separate JSON locale data and describes conversion from PO files.
sources.limits: Applications must supply converted locale catalogues and correct plural metadata; no dated pre-cutoff version was verified. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: unknown. Original read and any failures remain in runs/B/C20.json.
